meta.verificationNote: Domain names, the 6/31 structure, adjustment dimensions (personalisation/frequency/intensity), the 4 adjustment-level names, and the supporting-information rules below are drawn directly from the current published Department policy and guidance pages listed above (last checked on the date shown). The Functional Needs Domain Table and Level of Adjustment documents are published only as PDFs that could not be machine-verified word-for-word when this content was built. The starter 'activities' listed under each domain are ILLUSTRATIVE PLACEHOLDERS ONLY, are NOT verified against the official Functional Needs Domain Table, and must be reviewed/replaced by a school admin via Admin → Content before being relied on for an actual profile meeting.

adjustmentDimensions.name: Personalisation
adjustmentDimensions.description: The extent to which adjustments are tailored in response to the student's functional needs.

adjustmentDimensions.name: Frequency
adjustmentDimensions.description: The occurrence of adjustments over time.

adjustmentDimensions.name: Intensity
adjustmentDimensions.description: The amount and type of resources required to implement the adjustment, including planning and collaboration, staff support, tools and equipment.

adjustmentLevels.name: Differentiated
adjustmentLevels.generalDescription: Generally reflects lower personalisation, frequency and intensity than the levels below. Often able to be described verbally at the profile meeting without extensive documentation.

adjustmentLevels.name: Supplementary
adjustmentLevels.generalDescription: Reflects a degree of personalisation, frequency and intensity above differentiated. Like the differentiated level, may often be described verbally without extensive documentation.

adjustmentLevels.name: Substantial
adjustmentLevels.generalDescription: Reflects a higher degree of personalisation, frequency and/or intensity. Supporting documentation is generally required to confirm this level matches the student's demonstrated functional needs.

adjustmentLevels.name: Extensive
adjustmentLevels.generalDescription: Reflects the highest degree of personalisation, frequency and/or intensity. Supporting documentation is generally required to confirm this level matches the student's demonstrated functional needs.

supportingInformation.principle: Supporting information should be existing school-based documentation, not created solely for the profile. Quality and relevance matter more than quantity.
goodSources: Individual Education Plan (IEP) / Individual Learning Plan (ILP)
Teaching and learning program / classroom planning documents
A summary snapshot of strengths, aspirations and adjustments in place
Transition Learning and Development Statements / transition plans
Other student-specific plans (communication, transfer/mobility, meal/toileting, safety plans)
Specialist/allied health reports where already held by the school
NDIS plan or therapy/assessment/progress reports (optional, not a substitute for school-based evidence)
excludedSources: Budget information relating to NDIS plans
Whole excerpts/records showing behavioural concerns or presentations
Documents disclosing details of abuse or trauma
notes: Educational management system notes (e.g. Compass, Sentral) must be reviewed for relevance and privacy before use – only 'need to know' adjustment information should be included.
Digital evidence (photo/video) should not be used to highlight a student's disability or presentation and must have appropriate consent.

No third-party software (other than the DIFS Portal) is accredited by the Department for managing the profile process – school approval, privacy impact assessment and ST4S risk review are required before use of any such tool.

lowAttendancePathway.note: Facilitators apply a flexible approach for students with low attendance, placing more emphasis on evidence of ongoing adjustment needs and re-engagement planning. Tier 3 funding may not be allocated if the student is not currently attending school.

processSteps: Identify the student to undertake a profile, with parents/carers and/or the SSG
Register a profile request with the facilitator service (DIFS)
Complete the profile request: screening questions, profile information form, and upload supporting information
Prepare for the meeting (school, parents/carers and student)
Participate in the meeting, led by a trained Disability Inclusion Facilitator
Provide additional supporting information if requested (within 5 school days)
Receive the finalised profile and School Resource Notification via the DIFS Portal
Discuss the finalised report with the SSG and update the IEP
Continue planning, implementing and monitoring adjustments regardless of outcome

nccd.note: The Disability Inclusion Profile and the Nationally Consistent Collection of Data on School Students with Disability (NCCD) are related but separate processes. A Profile outcome does not automatically determine a student's NCCD adjustment level, and evidence gathered here may separately help inform NCCD professional judgement.
